# Turns article titles into lowercase, hyphen-separated URL slugs.
module Slugify
  SEPARATOR = '-'
  COMBINING_MARKS = /\p{Mn}/
  NON_ALPHANUMERIC = /[^a-z0-9]+/

  # Example: Slugify.call('Héllo, Wörld!') # => 'hello-world'
  def self.call(title, max_length: nil)
    slug = title.to_s
                .unicode_normalize(:nfkd)
                .gsub(COMBINING_MARKS, '')
                .downcase
                .gsub(NON_ALPHANUMERIC, SEPARATOR)
                .delete_prefix(SEPARATOR)
                .delete_suffix(SEPARATOR)

    return slug unless max_length

    # Cutting can leave a trailing separator, so strip it again.
    slug[0, max_length].delete_suffix(SEPARATOR)
  end
end

# Turns article titles into lowercase, hyphen-separated URL slugs.
module Slugify
  class Error < StandardError; end
  class InvalidTitle < Error; end

  DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH = 80
  MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 500

  # Accented letters are reduced to their ASCII base letter; any other
  # non-alphanumeric run becomes a single hyphen. Raises InvalidTitle when
  # the input is not a usable string or contains nothing sluggable.
  def self.slugify(title, max_length: DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH)
    validate!(title, max_length)

    slug = title.unicode_normalize(:nfkd).gsub(/\p{Mn}/, '').downcase
    slug = slug.gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, '-').gsub(/\A-+|-+\z/, '')
    slug = slug[0, max_length].sub(/-+\z/, '')

    raise InvalidTitle, "title has no letters or digits (length #{title.length})" if slug.empty?

    slug
  end

  def self.validate!(title, max_length)
    raise InvalidTitle, "expected a String title, got #{title.class}" unless title.is_a?(String)
    raise InvalidTitle, 'title has invalid encoding' unless title.valid_encoding?
    raise InvalidTitle, "title longer than #{MAX_TITLE_LENGTH} characters" if title.length > MAX_TITLE_LENGTH
    raise ArgumentError, "max_length must be a positive Integer, got #{max_length.inspect}" unless
      max_length.is_a?(Integer) && max_length.positive?
  end
  private_class_method :validate!
end

require 'logger'

# Writes rows to a CSV file and logs progress every 100 rows.
class CsvExporter
  class Error < StandardError; end
  class InvalidRows < Error; end
  class WriteError < Error; end

  PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100

  # The default logger discards output so the gem stays silent unless the host app injects one.
  def initialize(path:, headers: nil, logger: Logger.new(nil))
    @path = path
    @headers = headers
    @logger = logger
  end

  # Returns the number of data rows written.
  def export(rows)
    validate_rows!(rows)
    started = monotonic_now
    count = write_rows(rows)
    @logger.info(event: 'csv_export.finished', path: @path, rows: count,
                 duration_ms: ((monotonic_now - started) * 1000).round)
    count
  rescue SystemCallError => e
    raise WriteError, "could not write CSV to #{@path.inspect}: #{e.message}"
  end

  private

  def write_rows(rows)
    count = 0
    CSV.open(@path, 'w') do |csv|
      csv << @headers if @headers
      rows.each do |row|
        csv << row
        count += 1
        report_progress(count) if (count % PROGRESS_INTERVAL).zero?
      end
    end
    count
  end

  def report_progress(count)
    @logger.info(event: 'csv_export.progress', path: @path, rows: count)
  end

  def validate_rows!(rows)
    return if rows.respond_to?(:each)

    raise InvalidRows, "rows must respond to each, got #{rows.class}"
  end

  def monotonic_now
    Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'csv'
require 'logger'

# Writes rows to a CSV file and logs progress every PROGRESS_INTERVAL rows.
class CsvExporter
  class Error < StandardError; end
  class InvalidPath < Error; end
  class InvalidRow < Error; end
  class WriteFailed < Error; end

  PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100

  def initialize(path:, headers: nil, logger: Logger.new(nil))
    @path = validate_path!(path)
    @headers = headers
    @logger = logger
  end

  # Writes every row and returns the number of rows written.
  # Rows are arrays of values; the optional headers are written first.
  def export(rows)
    started = monotonic_now
    count = write_rows(rows)
    log_finished(count, started)
    count
  end

  private

  def validate_path!(path)
    unless path.is_a?(String) || path.respond_to?(:to_path)
      raise InvalidPath, "path must be a String or Pathname, got #{path.class}"
    end

    path = path.to_s
    raise InvalidPath, 'path must not be empty' if path.empty?

    path
  end

  def write_rows(rows)
    count = 0
    CSV.open(@path, 'w') do |csv|
      csv << @headers if @headers
      rows.each do |row|
        csv << validate_row!(row, count)
        count += 1
        log_progress(count) if (count % PROGRESS_INTERVAL).zero?
      end
    end
    count
  rescue SystemCallError, IOError => e
    raise WriteFailed, "could not write #{@path}: #{e.message}"
  end

  def validate_row!(row, index)
    return row if row.is_a?(Array)

    raise InvalidRow, "row #{index} must be an Array, got #{row.class}"
  end

  def log_progress(count)
    @logger.info(event: 'csv_export.progress', path: @path, rows_written: count)
  end

  def log_finished(count, started)
    duration_ms = ((monotonic_now - started) * 1000).round
    @logger.info(event: 'csv_export.finished', path: @path, rows_written: count,
                 duration_ms: duration_ms)
  end

  def monotonic_now
    Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
  end
end

feat(payments): retry webhook handler with exponential backoff

Transient failures in the payment webhook handler, such as timeouts
from downstream services, caused events to be dropped until the
provider redelivered them. That delayed order confirmation and made
failures hard to trace.

Retry the handler a bounded number of times with exponential backoff
and jitter. Each retry is logged at warn level, and the original error
is raised after the final attempt. Only idempotent processing steps are
retried, so a repeated delivery cannot charge or credit twice.

ruly.reply:
feat(webhooks): add exponential backoff retry to payment handler

Payment webhook deliveries failed permanently on the first transient
error, such as a timeout or a 5xx from the provider, so a brief outage
could leave orders unconfirmed until someone replayed the events by
hand.

Retry failed handler runs with exponential backoff and jitter, up to a
fixed maximum number of attempts. Non-retryable errors, such as
validation failures and 4xx responses, still fail immediately. Each
attempt logs the attempt number, the delay and the error class, and
exhausting the retries emits a failure metric and an error report with
the event id.

Risk: handlers can now run more than once for the same event, so they
must be idempotent. The existing handler already deduplicates on event
id.

Rejected a queue-based redelivery design as more infrastructure than
this problem needs today.
